Severynivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Severynivka, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though presumed late 19th century; the only map showing it, a 1927 Russian topographic map, mislabels it as a Christian Orthodox cemetery - an apparent error, since tombstones with Hebrew inscriptions were found on the site. It was presumably demolished after WWII. Jewish community mentions date to the mid-19th century, with a synagogue by 1865; population reached 234 (20%) by 1897, and a pogrom struck the village in 1905. Jews owned 10 market stalls by 1914; further Civil War-era pogrom violence struck 1918-1920. Population reached 600 by 1939 census, though the community's specific WWII fate remains undocumented.
